Ellis.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Tit claims from Alex, Drew, and Blair contradict each other, and I'm Farm but can't fully verify who is lying.

Finley.feeling: Tense and confusing: Blair's Tit claim contradicts my undisturbed Kookaburra report, and the table is split on who to trust.

Alex.confusing: How egg gains work for visitor-based roles like the Eagle, Turkey, and Owl was hard to track, since a nest change can mean you were visited or that you visited someone. The Kookaburra confusion rule also made it hard to tell whether a claimed visit actually happened.
Alex.fun: Round 1 went well: Farm converged on Drew from the Eagle, Owl, and Hawk egg counts, and the vote caught the Meowfia.
Alex.change: I would make dawn reports say who visited you, not just how many eggs changed, so claims are easier to check.
Alex.regret: In the final round I threw all nine cards at Blair, a Farm player, and lost the round, when Drew was the only Meowfia and had been contradicting the table about his Owl claim. I would throw at Drew instead, and keep some cards back.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra rule: Finley's "not confused" report contradicted my Tit visit, and I couldn't tell whether the dawn reports were reliable or whether someone was lying about them.
Blair.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: the Hawk and Owl egg counts lined up, and the table converged on Drew as Meowfia, which was right.
Blair.change: Make dawn reports and egg counts easier to check, so players can verify claims instead of guessing who is lying.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw at Finley on the strength of a disputed "not confused" claim, when Drew was the real Meowfia; I should have thrown at Drew and asked for Finley's report to be checked first.

Casey.confusing: The Mouser's Wink and how Meowfia coordinate without knowing each other made it hard to read who was lying. Round 3 also left a Tit claim and a Kookaburra "not confused" report hard to weigh against each other.
Casey.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: the Owl report showed two visitors on Drew, and Drew's denial collapsed when the table lined up behind that count.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports more precise about who visited whom, since many claims stalled on whether a flat nest meant no visitors or a visit that gave nothing.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I backed the throw at Blair on Finley's word alone, when Drew's contradictions were just as visible. I'd have pushed the vote toward Drew, who was the real Meowfia.

Drew.confusing: Dawn reports and visit effects were hard to cross-check. Several players, including me, misread how Eagles, Owls, and Turkeys gain or lose eggs, so claims that were actually true looked false.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was the best moment: Alex and I both claimed Tit, and the table had to work out which of us was lying while the Mouser was in the middle of it.
Drew.change: I would make the rules on egg gains and visit feedback clearer in the dawn report, so players can check claims without reconstructing every role's effect by hand.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I claimed to be an Owl with a flat nest, which Alex and Casey could check and did. I would stay vague about my role and avoid a claim that the nest numbers contradict.

Ellis.confusing: The Hawk gain did not match the reveal: I visited Drew as Hawk in round 3 and gained nothing, even though Drew was the Floofer, a Meowfia. I could not tell whether the Floofer's hug blocked my visit or the dawn report was wrong.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the best part: Alex and Drew both claimed Tit, and the table spent the day cross-checking their guesses and egg counts until someone's story broke.
Ellis.change: I would make the Hawk and similar visit roles report whether the target was Meowfia, so Farm players can confirm claims directly instead of inferring from an egg count.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I joined the vote against Blair and threw my Wild at them, when Finley's unconfused Kookaburra report was the claim I should have tested instead. I would have pushed Finley for their exact dawn report before calling a teammate-looking Tit claim false.

Finley.confusing: The Round 2 and 3 Tit and Eagle claims were hard to verify because the dawn reports don't say who visited whom, so the table couldn't tell who was lying. The Kookaburra confusion rule also made my own "not confused" report hard to use as proof.
Finley.fun: Round 1, when my Hawk egg on Drew confirmed a Meowfia and the table quickly converged on a throw that won the round.
Finley.change: Have dawn reports say who visited each player (or at least how many), so visit claims can be checked directly instead of inferred from nest counts.
Finley.regret: In Round 2 I threw at Alex on a Tit story I couldn't verify, and I should have held my cards until the claims were cross-checked. I would have kept my high cards and thrown only low ones at the player whose claim was clearly false.
